A-League Men: Unite Round at Allianz Stadium, Moore Park. Gates open at 4:30pm, Perth Glory v Western United kick-off 5.30pm, Newcastle Jets v Central Coast Mariners kick-off 8pm, finish around 10pm. 

Traffic will be heavy in the area as fans travel to the match during the busy Friday evening peak. Motorists should allow extra travel time on roads approaching and around Moore Park including the Eastern Distributor, Moore Park Rd, Cleveland St, Anzac Pde and Lang Rd.

Changed traffic conditions:

  • Driver Avenue will be partially closed outside the stadium from 3.30pm and will reopen once crowds have safely cleared the area. No through-traffic will be available on Driver Avenue, however access to EP3 grass car park and drop-off areas maintained from Lang Road.  
  • Special event clearways will be in effect on roads in Moore Park and surrounding areas from 6am to 11pm on sections of Cleveland St and from 3pm to 11pm on Albion St, Fitzroy St and Moore Park Rd.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

Santa's Sydney Sleigh Ride in the Sydney CBD. Events start from 6.30pm and the Sleigh Ride will start at Customs House Square near Circular Quay at 8.10pm, travel along Pitt St and arrive at Martin Pl at approx. 8.20pm. The sleigh then leaves Martin Pl at 8.35pm, arriving at Town Hall at 8.45pm.

Pitt St will be closed between Hunter St and King St from 5pm to 10.30pm to safely facilitate the event. There will be no vehicle access for residents and businesses during this time, however access in and out of carparks along Pitt Street will be maintained.  Access into and out of the Fullerton Hotel will also be maintained by NSW Police and traffic controllers.

Traffic in the CBD and on approaches to Pitt Street will be heavy before, during and after the event. Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time and watch out for pedestrians in the area.

More than 800 trucks and 900 motorbikes will form part of the annual i98 Illawarra convoy travelling from Appin and Bulli Tops to finish near Shellharbour Airport in Albion Park Rail. Motorbikes will leave from West Cliff Colliery, Appin from 8:15am, trucks will leave from Maddens Plains at 8.30am.

The convoy will travel via Appin Rd, Old Princes Hwy, M1 Princes Mwy, Masters Rd, Five Islands Rd, King St, Windang Rd, Shellharbour Rd, Lake Entrance Road, New Lake Entrance Rd and Princes Hwy. The convoy will finish at the Convoy shop, corner of Airport Rd and Princes Hwy, Albion Park Rail. Bikes will arrive from 9.15am and trucks from 10am.

Motorists may experience traffic delays along the convoy route. 

Speed reductions will be in effect at various times and locations between 4.30am and 3pm on sections of Appin Rd, M1 Princes Mwy and Princes Hwy.

The Old Princes Highway at Madden Plains will be closed between Helensburgh and Maddens Plains while trucks form up to participate in the convoy.

The right-hand turn from Old Mount Ousley Rd onto the M1 Princes Mwy/Mount Ousley Rd will be closed between 7am and 12pm. The convoy will travel in one lane along the route. 

Motorists are advised to take care as they share roads with the convoy vehicles and allow extra travel time in the area while changed traffic conditions are in place.
